notes.liri-wa: Tye kwene? asks where something is.

guidebook.intro: Learn the places in town and how to give directions, then ride a boda boda to where you need to go.

tips.title: Atye ka cito
body: **Cito** is to go. **Atye ka cito i cukul** is “I am going to school”; **Itye ka cito kwene?** asks “where are you going?”. **I** in front of a place means in, at or to.
Ask where something is with **tye kwene?**: **Ot yat tye kwene?** (where is the hospital?).

tips.title: Right, left, straight
body: **Tung lacuc** is the right side and **tung lacam** the left. **Lokke** (turn), **Cit atir** (go straight), **Cung kany** (stop here).
**Tera** (take me) is **ter** (take) with **-a** for me: **Tera i taun** (take me to town).

culture.title: Gulu and the roads north
body: Gulu is the biggest town in the north, with Kitgum and Pader further east. Boda bodas are the quickest way around town; agree on the fare before you get on.
